points.description: States that removing each electron decreases electron–electron repulsion (fewer electrons remain), and links this to a decrease in potential energy of the remaining electrons (so the remaining electrons are held more tightly / more energy needed for the next removal).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if decreased electron–electron repulsion is stated but not linked to decreased potential energy.

points.description: 3rd and 4th electrons are removed from the same n=3 shell, so they feel the same core charge and have the same radius; this is why their ionization energies (3231 and 4356) are similar in magnitude / only modestly different.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only same core charge or only same shell/radius is stated, or the claim is given without the link to similar values.

points.description: 5th electron is removed from the n=2 shell (inner shell), so it feels a higher core charge and has a smaller radius than the 3rd/4th electrons, so it is much closer to the nucleus and attracted much more strongly (hence the large jump to 16091).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only higher core charge or only smaller radius/inner shell is stated.

points.description: Correctly explains the relationship of potential energy to ionization energy: lower (more negative) potential energy, from greater attraction (Coulomb's law: higher core charge, smaller distance), means more energy is needed to remove the electron, so ionization energy is larger.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the link between attraction/potential energy and ionization energy is stated only partly or vaguely.

rubric.notes: Full marks need each specific claim stated with its cause-and-effect link: for example "same core charge" (not "similar attraction"), and potential energy linked to ionization energy. Part marks go to half-stated ideas, such as only the core charge or only the radius. A bare restatement of the data or a general definition of ionization energy earns nothing, and a wrong statement loses only the marks of its own point.
